text:
Maya: heads-up — AcmeCorp reported a sudden spike of 429s in production starting ~09:12 PDT. They say this started after a nightly job landed.
Quinn (AcmeCorp): we're getting ~10% of requests returning 429 with Retry-After and the app degrades. timeline: spike started 09:12, steady through 09:30. We tried retries but it floods again.
Maya: customer attached logs and a small repro curl they used. pasted below.
Quinn (AcmeCorp): curl sample:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_acmecorp_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":256}'
```
Quinn (AcmeCorp): response headers they saw:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1712987580
```
Sam: initial hypothesis — looks like per-minute RPM quota hit (requests/min) not TPM. X-RateLimit-Limit 6000 suggests a per-minute bucket at some scope. Need to check whether that header is per-API-key or per-org.
Jin: I'll pull quota mappings for the token. @Sam can you paste the API key suffix? we can look up the tenant config.
Maya: API key suffix from customer: acme_9f3a
Sam: got it. Checking internal ledger...
rate-limit-bot: lookup: key_suffix=acme_9f3a scope=org:acme id=org_87342 plan=team
rate-limit-bot: quotas: rpm=6000, tpm=200000, burst_window=10s, outstanding_requests_limit=120
Sam: confirms org-level RPM=6000. That matches header. The job QE ran choked the bucket. Looks like they have a high TPM but RPM capped lower — bursts of short requests can exhaust RPM quickly.
Maya: customer note: their nightly job parallelized 50 workers hitting /generate with small prompts at 1 request/sec each for ~3 minutes. rough math: 50 rps -> 3000 rpm but they also have app traffic pushing it over.
Jin: key insight: RPM counts requests, TPM counts tokens. Small prompt bursts with many requests -> RPM hit even if token budget remains.
Sam: recommended actions to customer: 1) add jittered exponential backoff on 429 with Retry-After, 2) smooth bursts with local client-side queueing, 3) consider batching requests into single calls when possible, 4) request temporary RPM increase or change to Dedicated.
Maya: customer asked how to best implement backoff. Suggested snippet:
```
// pseudo-js retry w/ jitter
async function fetchWithRetry(req, retries = 5) {
  for (let i=0;i<retries;i++){
    const res = await fetch(req)
    if (res.status !== 429) return res
    const ra = parseInt(res.headers.get('Retry-After') || '1',10)
    const jitter = Math.random()*1000
    await sleep((Math.pow(2,i)*ra*1000) + jitter)
  }
  throw new Error('exhausted retries')
}
```
Quinn (AcmeCorp): can you tell us if this is a global limit across the whole org or per-model route? We have multiple services using the same key.
Sam: it's org-level RPM by default for team plan. Could be per-route if they've configured per-route quotas, but ledger shows org-level.
Jin: also check autoscaling/backpressure: if their deploy fanout causes many concurrent inflight requests the platform's outstanding_requests_limit (120) can trigger queuing and 429s even before RPM hits. We saw outstanding_requests spikes in metrics correlating with 09:12.
Maya: I attached a grafana screenshot the customer provided showing spike in request rate and concurrent inflight count.
Sam: actionable item for infra: fetch traces for org_87342 between 1712987460-1712987700. look at inflight, token consumption, and model routing. I'll take traces.
Jin: investigating traces now. initial find: many short requests (<300ms) with no pipelining—lots of tiny calls.
rate-limit-bot: trace-extract: traces=4800 span_hits=1200 peak_inflight=138 rpm_peak=7250
Sam: RPM peak 7250 > quota 6000. That explains the 429s. also peak_inflight 138 > outstanding limit 120 -> additional rejections.
Maya: proposed customer-facing summary: "Your org hit the configured RPM quota (6000) during a nightly job; the short parallel requests caused a burst that exceeded both the RPM bucket and the outstanding inflight threshold. Result: many 429s with Retry-After set."
Quinn (AcmeCorp): we need a short-term workaround while we refactor the job.
Lena (Support Lead): options: "1) temporary quota bump for 24h, 2) recommend batching + client backoff, 3) enable token-based burst smoothing if available." Which do you want Maya to offer?
Maya: offer (1) 24h bump + (2) implementation guidance. Also include logging guidance: check X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After in app metrics.
Quinn (AcmeCorp): yes please do the 24h bump. Also can you confirm whether Dedicated would eliminate this behavior?
Sam: Dedicated removes shared org rate limits and gives reserved capacity; you'll get higher guaranteed RPM and different controls for burst handling. Recommend Dedicated for sustained high-throughput jobs.
Jin: I'll patch the customer's org quota for 24 hours: old=6000 rpm, new=9000 rpm, expires=1713074054
rate-limit-bot: quota-update: org=org_87342 rpm:6000->9000 expires_at=1713074054 by=jin
Sam: follow-up checklist for internal team:
- [ ] Confirm quota bump applied and customer notified
- [ ] Provide sample backoff + batching doc (link to internal KB)
- [ ] Monitor metrics for next 6 hours and rollback if misuse
- [ ] Sales/AE loop in for Dedicated evaluation
Maya: I messaged Quinn with the temporary bump and the backoff snippet. Quinn said they'll throttle the job tonight and adopt batching next week.
Quinn (AcmeCorp): thanks y'all. we'll confirm after tonight's run. appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
Lena (Support Lead): closing notes: mark as resolved when no further 429s within 24h window. add credit only if customer had visible production impact and on a case-by-case basis.
Maya: will update thread after observing tonight. closing for now.
